{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In [[algebra]], more specifically in [[algebraic K-theory]], the '''suspension''' <math>\Sigma R</math> of a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' is given by<ref>Weibel, III, Ex. 1.15</ref> <math>\Sigma(R) = C(R)/M(R)</math> where <math>C(R)</math> is the ring of all [[infinite matrix|infinite matrices]] with entries in ''R'' having only finitely many nonzero elements in each row or column and <math>M(R)</math> is its [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] of [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]] having only finitely many nonzero elements. It is an analog of [[suspension (topology)|suspension]] in [[topology]].

One then has: <math>K_i(R) \simeq K_{i+1}(\Sigma R)</math>.
